notes: UK-wide rules (England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland) from Companies House and HMRC; devolved differences such as Scottish income tax rates don't change these deadlines.

items.name: Confirmation Statement (CS01)
items.rule: Within 14 days after the end of each 12-month review period (the anniversary of incorporation, or of the last statement)
items.applies: Every company and LLP, including dormant ones
items.description: Confirms the registered office, officers, people with significant control, shareholders and SIC codes, plus the registered email address and lawful-purpose statement; the fee is paid with it.

items.name: Annual Accounts to Companies House
items.rule: 9 months after the accounting reference date (first accounts: 21 months after incorporation)
items.description: Statutory accounts are filed every year even if the company is dormant or made a loss; late filing penalties start at £150 and double if late two years running.

items.name: Annual Accounts to Companies House (PLC)
items.rule: 6 months after the accounting reference date
items.description: Public companies have a shorter filing deadline than private companies, and their accounts must be laid before an AGM.

items.name: Annual General Meeting (PLC)
items.rule: Within 6 months beginning with the day after the accounting reference date
items.description: A PLC must hold an AGM every year, within 6 months after its financial year end.

items.name: Corporation Tax Payment
items.rule: 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period (large companies pay in quarterly instalments)
items.description: Companies with profits over £1.5 million pay by quarterly instalments starting in the 7th month of the period; everyone else pays 9 months and 1 day after the period ends.

items.name: Company Tax Return (CT600)
items.rule: 12 months after the end of the accounting period
items.applies: Every company within the charge to Corporation Tax
items.description: Filed online with iXBRL-tagged accounts and computations, even when no tax is owed.

items.name: Register for Corporation Tax
items.rule: Within 3 months of starting to trade
items.description: Tell HMRC the company has become active (trading, buying, selling, employing or advertising).

items.name: Report Changes to Companies House (officers, PSCs, registered office)
items.rule: Within 14 days of the change
items.description: Appointments and resignations of directors or LLP members, changes of people with significant control and of the registered office must be filed promptly; new directors and PSCs must also verify their identity with Companies House.

items.name: Identity Verification for Directors and PSCs
items.rule: New directors before appointment; existing directors and PSCs by the company's next confirmation statement after 18 November 2025
items.applies: Directors, LLP members and people with significant control
items.description: Under the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023, everyone who controls a company must verify their identity with Companies House and provide a personal code.

items.name: Self Assessment Tax Return
items.rule: 31 January after the end of the tax year (5 April) for online returns; 31 October for paper
items.description: Business profits are reported on the individual return (SA100 with self-employment or partnership pages).

items.name: Self Assessment Balancing Payment and Payments on Account
items.rule: 31 January and 31 July
items.applies: Individuals whose last tax bill was over £1,000 (unless most was taxed at source)
items.description: The balancing payment plus the first payment on account are due 31 January; the second payment on account is due 31 July.

items.name: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax — Quarterly Updates
items.rule: 7 August, 7 November, 7 February and 7 May
items.applies: Sole traders with qualifying income over £50,000 (from 6 April 2026; £30,000 from April 2027)
items.description: Digital records and quarterly updates through compatible software, followed by an end-of-year final declaration by 31 January.

items.name: Partnership Tax Return (SA800)
items.rule: 31 January after the end of the tax year (online)
items.description: The LLP's return shows each member's share of profit; each member then reports it on their own return.

items.name: Register for Self Assessment
items.rule: By 5 October after the end of the tax year in which the business (or LLP membership) started
items.applies: Sole traders and new LLP members
items.description: Registering late can lead to failure-to-notify penalties.

items.name: VAT Registration
items.rule: Within 30 days of the end of the month in which taxable turnover for the last 12 months went over £90,000
items.description: You must also register if you expect to go over £90,000 in the next 30 days alone.

items.name: VAT Return and Payment (quarterly)
items.rule: 1 calendar month and 7 days after the end of each VAT quarter (quarters as set by HMRC; we assume they follow your financial year)
items.description: Returns are filed through Making Tax Digital software; payment is due by the same date.

items.name: VAT Return and Payment (monthly)
items.rule: 1 calendar month and 7 days after the end of each month
items.description: Returns are filed through Making Tax Digital software; payment is due by the same date.

items.name: VAT Return (Annual Accounting Scheme)
items.rule: 2 months after the end of the VAT accounting year (interim payments during the year)
items.applies: Businesses using the VAT Annual Accounting Scheme
items.description: One return a year, with 9 monthly or 3 quarterly interim payments based on the previous year's VAT.

items.name: Register as an Employer (PAYE)
items.rule: Before the first payday (up to 2 months ahead)
items.description: Registering sets up the PAYE reference used for all payroll submissions.

items.name: Full Payment Submission (FPS)
items.rule: On or before every payday
items.description: Real Time Information: each pay run is reported to HMRC on or before the day employees are paid.

items.name: PAYE and National Insurance Payment
items.rule: 22nd of the month after each tax month ends on the 5th (19th if paying by cheque); quarterly if under £1,500 a month
items.description: Income tax, employee and employer National Insurance and student loan deductions, less any Employment Allowance.

items.name: Employer Payment Summary (EPS)
items.rule: By the 19th of the following tax month, when there is something to claim or report
items.description: Used to claim Employment Allowance or statutory pay recovery, or to tell HMRC no employees were paid in a month.

items.name: P60s to Employees
items.rule: 31 May
items.description: Every employee on the payroll at 5 April receives a P60 summarising the tax year's pay and deductions.

items.name: P11D and P11D(b) (benefits in kind)
items.rule: 6 July (Class 1A National Insurance paid by 22 July)
items.applies: Employers providing benefits or expenses not payrolled
items.description: Reports benefits such as company cars and private medical insurance; Class 1A NIC on them is paid by 22 July.

items.name: Workplace Pension Auto-Enrolment and Re-Declaration
items.rule: Duties start on the first employee's start date; declaration of compliance within 5 months; re-enrolment and re-declaration every 3 years
items.description: Eligible staff must be enrolled in a qualifying pension scheme with minimum contributions, and compliance declared to The Pensions Regulator.

items.name: Transfer Pricing Records
items.rule: Kept in support of the Company Tax Return
items.applies: Large companies with related-party transactions (small and medium-sized enterprises are generally exempt)
items.description: Large groups must price transactions with related parties at arm's length and keep evidence; groups with €750 million+ turnover also keep a master file and local file.
